notes: Fast bowling is the most heavily studied cricket action, yet almost none of it converts into scoreable bands here, for two separate reasons. FIRST, the best-known quantitative thresholds are INJURY thresholds - shoulder counter-rotation >30 deg for mixed action, front-knee flexion <30 deg at FFC elevating lumbar loading - and this app must not make injury claims (docs/ACCURACY.md). Encoding an injury threshold as a technique band would launder a safety judgement into a form score. SECOND, the performance findings that remain are reported as correlations rather than normative ranges: elitefastbowlers2024 gives front knee angle at release correlating with ball speed at r = 0.40, which tells you a direction but not a target. A correlation is not a band. Everything here is therefore unscored pending a source that reports normative ranges for a technique variable, free of injury framing.

bowling.front_knee_angle_ffc.notes: The available threshold (knee flexion <30 deg at FFC, i.e. >150 deg in this convention) comes from lumbar-loading research. Using it as a technique band would be an injury claim in disguise. Needs a performance-framed normative source.

bowling.front_knee_angle_br.notes: elitefastbowlers2024 reports r = 0.40 with ball release speed and that faster bowlers release with a more extended front knee - a direction, not a target range.

bowling.front_knee_change_ffc_br.notes: Bracing versus collapse. Highest-value gap in this template: it is a difference of two well-measured sagittal angles, so measurement error partly cancels, and it captures the mechanism elitefastbowlers2024 describes. Worth sourcing first.

bowling.trunk_lateral_flexion_br.notes: Demoted from Tier A on review. abraham2025opencap measured lateral flexion at 9.10 deg RMSE, but with three cameras. It is a frontal-plane motion, so on the single side-on camera this app specifies it points toward and away from the lens and is foreshortened - the published RMSE does not transfer to our capture geometry. Requires the optional front-on angle. The published values are also framed around lumbar loading rather than technique quality.

bowling.interval_bfc_ffc.notes: elitefastbowlers2024 associates reduced back-foot contact time with faster release but reports no normative interval. This is a temporal metric so it carries the highest score weight once a band exists.

bowling.interval_ffc_br.notes: Requires the 120 fps capture floor to be meaningful - see metric_tiers min_fps.

bowling.runup_final_stride_tempo.notes: Run-up speed is associated with release speed, but tempo as a ratio of final stride durations has no published band.

bowling.delivery_stride_length_norm.notes: Published stride-length work reports absolute metres alongside front-foot kinetics, not stature-normalised ranges.

bowling.trunk_forward_flexion_br.notes: Promoted to Tier A on review. This is a sagittal-plane motion, so it lies IN the image plane on the side-on camera the capture protocol specifies - the one trunk angle this geometry measures well. elitefastbowlers2024 associates greater trunk flexion with faster release, but reports a correlation rather than a normative range, so it remains unscored.

bowling.head_over_front_foot_ffc.notes: Widely coached, no quantitative normative band located.
